command_verbs.name: Find (a value, an expression, or a vector)
command_verbs.typical_response: A value or expression with whatever work the accompanying instruction demands; alone the verb does not compel shown work, and the rubrics then award the answer point with or without supporting work.
scoring_evidence: sg-26:18 Q5(A) awards the answer point for an unsupported value while the antiderivative point needs work
sg-25:18 Q4(c) asks to find two values and scores each as an unsupported answer with a label
sg-22:7 Q2(b) asks to find speed and an acceleration vector and requires the setup to be evident

command_verbs.name: Determine (whether, or which case holds)
command_verbs.typical_response: A decision between named alternatives, carried by an analysis point plus a conclusion point.
scoring_evidence: sg-24:2 Q1(d) asks to determine whether a rate is changing at an increasing rate and awards an answer with reason
sg-23:10 Q3(c) asks to determine overestimate or underestimate and pairs a second derivative point with a reason point
sg-21:24 Q6(c) asks to determine the radius of convergence and requires the radius to be stated explicitly

command_verbs.name: Evaluate
command_verbs.typical_response: A closed-form or numerical value obtained by carrying the computation through, normally scored as an antiderivative point plus an answer point.
scoring_evidence: sg-26:18 Q5(A) evaluate a definite integral, scored antiderivative then answer
sg-26:20 Q5(D) evaluate an improper integral, scored limit notation, antiderivative, answer
sg-23:17 Q5(b) evaluate an improper integral or show it diverges

command_verbs.name: Estimate
command_verbs.typical_response: A value derived from given data rather than from a closed form, with the difference and quotient or the sum visible.
scoring_evidence: sg-24:2 Q1(a) estimate a derivative from a table, scored estimate with supporting work plus units
sg-21:2 Q1(a) estimate a derivative from a table and interpret it with units
sg-22:13 Q4(a) approximate a second derivative from a table, requiring at least a difference and a quotient

command_verbs.name: Approximate
command_verbs.typical_response: A value from a stated approximation method, with the method's structure visible; the rubrics score the form of the method and the resulting value separately.
scoring_evidence: sg-25:13 Q3(c) approximate an integral with a trapezoidal sum, scored form then value
sg-26:3 Q1(B) approximate an integral with a midpoint sum, scored form then approximation with supporting work
sg-25:23 Q5(D) approximate a function value by Euler's method, scored first step then answer

command_verbs.name: Explain why
command_verbs.typical_response: A written argument naming the property that makes the claim hold, tied to the object the prompt names.
scoring_evidence: sg-26:10 Q3(A) explain why a figure could not be a slope field, scored as a single explanation point
sg-26:11 lists communication failures that do not earn the explanation point
sg-26:11 allows a local argument at any point of the field in place of a global one
command_verbs.notes: One question in the corpus read uses this stem, so tagged single-source.

command_verbs.name: Justify your answer
command_verbs.typical_response: A global argument, not merely a local one; sign analysis across the whole interval, a candidates test at every candidate, or theorem hypotheses plus conclusion.
scoring_evidence: sg-25:5 Q1(D) a local First or Second Derivative Test argument does not earn the justification point
sg-25:19 Q4(d) a candidates test must evaluate at every candidate and no others
sg-23:15 Q4(d) a response that does not consider both endpoints does not earn the justification point

command_verbs.name: Give a reason for your answer
command_verbs.verb: Give a reason for your answer
command_verbs.typical_response: A shorter written reason than a justification, but one that must be tied to the object the prompt names rather than to a derived object.
scoring_evidence: sg-25:17 Q4(b) the reason must tie to the given graph, and reasoning from the second derivative earns the answer point only
sg-26:15 Q4(B) the same split, with ambiguous terms such as the function rejected
sg-26:11 Q3(C) a concavity reason earns the reason point only when the sign point was earned

command_verbs.name: Give reasons for your answers
command_verbs.typical_response: Two separate conclusions each carrying its own reason, scored as separate points.
scoring_evidence: sg-26:17 Q4(D) awards one point for the minimum with reason and one for the maximum with reason
sg-26:17 special case where both locations are correct but the justification is insufficient earns one of the two
sg-23:7 Q2(c) asks for two findings in one part and scores three points across them
command_verbs.notes: The plural stem appears once in the corpus read, so tagged single-source.

command_verbs.name: Interpret the meaning of a value or expression in context
command_verbs.typical_response: A sentence in the context of the problem naming the quantity, its value where one is asked for, and the interval or instant it applies to.
scoring_evidence: sg-26:3 Q1(B) the interpretation must include the quantity that arrives and the interval
sg-23:2 Q1(a) must reference the accumulated quantity and the interval
sg-23:4 Q1(d) must give the changing rate and the instant, and sign language must match the presented value

command_verbs.name: Using correct units
command_verbs.typical_response: Units carried into the interpretation; the rubrics read them in the interpretation when they conflict with units on the value.
scoring_evidence: sg-23:2 Q1(a) pairs the instruction with an interpretation with units point
sg-21:3 states units need not be repeated but that conflicting units are read from the interpretation
sg-21:2 Q1(a) scores interpretation with units as one point

command_verbs.name: Indicate units of measure
command_verbs.typical_response: A separate units point, earned whether or not the units are attached to the numerical value.
scoring_evidence: sg-25:11 Q3(a) units earned whether or not attached to a value
sg-26:2 Q1(A) same wording, with a compact equivalent form accepted
sg-22:13 Q4(a) units may be written in any equivalent form but need a presented value

command_verbs.name: Show the setup for your calculations
command_verbs.verb: Show the setup for your calculations
command_verbs.typical_response: The expression that the calculator evaluated, written before the value; the rubrics score the setup and the value as separate points.
scoring_evidence: sg-25:2 Q1(a) average value formula point precedes the answer point
sg-26:9 Q2(D) same split for a polar average value
sg-25:7 Q2(b) integrand points precede the answer point

command_verbs.name: Show the work that leads to your answer
command_verbs.verb: Show the work that leads to your answer
command_verbs.typical_response: Intermediate steps rather than a finished value; unsupported answers are named in the rubrics as failing the work point.
scoring_evidence: sg-26:14 Q4(A) an unsupported answer earns the answer point but not the setup point
sg-25:11 Q3(a) the quotient template alone is not sufficient, a value must be produced
sg-23:10 Q3(b) an unsupported approximation does not earn the approximation point

command_verbs.name: Write, but do not evaluate, an expression or integral
command_verbs.typical_response: An unevaluated integral expression with correct limits and integrand; no numerical value is required or rewarded.
scoring_evidence: sg-26:19 Q5(B) form of integrand point plus answer point for the unevaluated integral
sg-26:19 Q5(C) form of arc length integral point plus answer point
sg-22:2 Q1(a) the response must be a definite integral with correct limits

command_verbs.name: Label your answers
command_verbs.typical_response: Each value tagged with the quantity it represents; unlabelled values earn nothing.
scoring_evidence: sg-25:18 Q4(c) unlabelled values earn neither point
sg-22:10 Q3(a) a single value must be labelled to earn any point
sg-23:6 Q2(a) components may be listed separately as long as they are labelled

command_verbs.name: Sketch a solution curve
command_verbs.typical_response: A drawn curve through the given point, consistent with the drawn slope segments and with any asymptote.
scoring_evidence: sg-23:9 Q3(a) the curve must pass through the point, reach near both edges, and lie below the equilibrium segments
sg-24:9 Q3(a) same single solution curve point
sg-23:9 states only the portion within the given field is considered
command_verbs.notes: Two documents in the corpus read carry this stem, so tagged single-source.

command_verbs.name: Use a derivative test to determine
command_verbs.verb: Use a derivative test to determine
command_verbs.typical_response: A classification of a critical point supported by first or second derivative analysis; the test need not be named, and a candidates test is explicitly rejected.
scoring_evidence: sg-26:8 Q2(C) the response must correctly classify the critical point with analysis using a derivative test
sg-26:8 states a candidates test is not sufficient justification for this point
sg-24:10 Q3(b) scores the sign consideration, the location, and the classification separately
command_verbs.notes: The explicit stem appears once in the corpus read, so tagged single-source.

command_verbs.name: Must there be a value, or is there a time, such that
command_verbs.verb: Must there be, or is there
command_verbs.typical_response: An existence claim built from a named theorem's hypotheses, the bracketing values, and an explicit yes.
scoring_evidence: sg-25:12 Q3(b) requires bracketing values, a continuity statement, and a yes
sg-26:5 Q1(D) states yes with the theorem named is not sufficient
sg-23:3 Q1(b) requires the difference point and rejects an appeal to the Intermediate Value Theorem

command_verbs.name: Show that a stated result holds
command_verbs.typical_response: A derivation ending on the stated target, or an inequality connecting a computed bound to the stated number.
scoring_evidence: sg-25:26 Q6(C) the verification point is earned by a chain landing on the given form
sg-25:22 Q5(c) the analysis point requires an explicit connection to the stated bound
sg-22:21 Q6(b) a response stating the error equals the bound does not earn the point

command_verbs.name: Using the ratio test, find the interval of convergence
command_verbs.typical_response: A ratio of consecutive terms, a limit, an interior interval, endpoint substitution, and endpoint analysis, scored as separate points.
scoring_evidence: sg-25:24 Q6(a) scores ratio, limit, interior, both endpoints, and analysis as five points
sg-22:20 Q6(a) scores the same sequence as four points
sg-21:24 Q6(c) scores ratio, limit, and radius

command_verbs.name: Use separation of variables to find a particular solution
command_verbs.typical_response: A separated equation, antiderivatives on both sides, a constant of integration resolved by the initial condition, and the solved function.
scoring_evidence: sg-26:13 Q3(D) states a response with no separation earns none of the five points
sg-23:12 Q3(d) states the same for its four points
sg-21:20 Q5(c) states a response with no constant of integration earns at most three of five

command_verbs.name: Use Euler's method with a stated number of steps
command_verbs.typical_response: The stated number of steps with the correct initial condition, step size, and derivative expression, followed by the approximation.
scoring_evidence: sg-25:23 Q5(D) requires the first step with correct initial condition, step size, and derivative expression
sg-24:17 Q5(c) requires two steps with at most one error
sg-21:19 Q5(b) allows a labelled table in place of explicit expressions

command_verbs.name: Use a named sum with the indicated subintervals to approximate
command_verbs.verb: Use a Riemann or trapezoidal sum with the indicated subintervals
command_verbs.typical_response: A sum of the named type over the named subintervals, with every factor visible; the sum's form and the resulting value score separately.
scoring_evidence: sg-25:13 Q3(c) requires three terms each a product of two factors, at least five of six correct
sg-26:3 Q1(B) the same five of six rule for a midpoint sum
sg-22:15 Q4(c) seven of eight factors for four subintervals

command_verbs.name: Use the Lagrange error bound to show
command_verbs.typical_response: The bound written with the maximum derivative, the factorial, and the distance power, then connected to the target by an inequality.
scoring_evidence: sg-25:22 Q5(c) scores the form of the error bound and the analysis separately
sg-23:20 Q6(b) scores the form and the explicit inequality separately
sg-25:22 rejects a response declaring the error equal to the bound
command_verbs.notes: Two documents in the corpus read carry this stem, so tagged single-source.

command_verbs.name: Write the first nonzero terms and the general term
command_verbs.verb: Write the first nonzero terms and the general term
command_verbs.typical_response: A stated count of nonzero terms plus a closed form for the general term, listed or inside a series.
scoring_evidence: sg-25:26 Q6(B) scores first three terms and the general term as separate points
sg-22:22 Q6(c) scores first four terms and the general term as separate points
sg-26:23 Q6(D) scores two terms then the remaining term for the combined series

command_verbs.name: Write the Taylor or Maclaurin polynomial of a stated degree
command_verbs.typical_response: A polynomial in powers of the centre, to the stated degree and no higher, with no trailing ellipsis.
scoring_evidence: sg-25:22 Q5(b) any terms of degree greater than two or a trailing ellipsis loses the remaining-term point
sg-23:19 Q6(a) the same rule for a fourth-degree polynomial
sg-23:21 Q6(c) the same rule for a second-degree polynomial

command_verbs.name: Round your answer to the nearest integer
command_verbs.verb: Round your answer to the nearest integer
command_verbs.typical_response: An integer answer, with the rubric also accepting several truncated and exact forms.
scoring_evidence: sg-26:4 Q1(C) accepts the rounded integer, several truncations, and the exact expression
sg-26:4 states units are not considered in scoring for this part
sg-22:3 Q1(b) by contrast rejects a value rounded to an integer where three decimals were required
command_verbs.notes: One instance of the explicit rounding instruction in the corpus read, so tagged single-source.

command_verbs.name: Write and evaluate a limit expression
command_verbs.typical_response: The limit written symbolically, then its value; arithmetic with infinity in place of the limit is treated as scratch work.
scoring_evidence: sg-25:4 Q1(c) scores the limit expression and the value as separate points
sg-25:4 states arithmetic with infinity is treated as scratch work for the value point
sg-25:4 states a limit taken on the function rather than its derivative blocks the value point
command_verbs.notes: One question in the corpus read carries this stem, so tagged single-source.
